 Disclaimer: The translations are mostly done through AI translator and might not be 100% accurate. 
 K 
 KB 
 03.11.2026. 08:18h 
 Four games in Florida at the start of the season, four losses - the "Kia Center" is still waiting for Orlando's first home win, just like our Nikola Vučević since he returned to the "magical" ranks.
 The Magic suffered another setback against Washington (103:94), and the Montenegrin basketball player scored seven points, grabbed six rebounds, and had one assist and one block in 13 and a half minutes.
 The best player on his team, which is 2-5, was Franz Wagner with 24 points, while the Wizards were led to victory by Anthony Davis with 27 points and nine rebounds.
 The Magic moving the ball to find Nikola Vucevic, who punishes with a three-pointer!! 🎯👌🏻 #NBA #MakeItMagic https://t.co/vsOYXBGsPv
— MagicLatam🎩🪄 (2-5) (@OrlandomagicLA) November 3, 2026 
 Vučević shot 3/1 from three-point range, while Orlando shot 39/11. The third quarter was particularly disastrous, with Sean Sweeney's team making 11 attempts from outside the 7,24 line and only making one. The coach of the Florida team, however, is not worried.
 "Nothing changes when it comes to the way we want to play. We want to attack the racket," said Sweeney, expecting Tristan da Silva and Desmond Bayne to hit open shots in the upcoming games that they missed against Washington.
 When it comes to the other matches from the previous night, Luka Dončić and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander were once again in charge of the show.
 The Slovenian maestro led the Los Angeles Lakers to a 138-117 win over Miami with 42 points, 13 assists and seven rebounds. The California giants are now 6-2 after Doncic, who averaged 43,4 points per game during that stretch, surpassed the 40-point mark for the fourth time in the last five games.
 Austin Reeves scored 27 points and Walker Kessler added 15 points and 15 rebounds for the Lakers. Giannis Antetokounmpo led Miami with 30 points, 12 rebounds and seven assists, while Klay Thompson added 19 points and Bam Adebayo had 16.
 Gilges-Alexander scored 43 points and hit a three-pointer to take the lead with 32,6 seconds left, as Oklahoma defeated Cleveland (117:112) in the first of two head-to-head matches.
 The Canadian didn't have memorable percentages (he made 35 field goals and hit 14), but that's the least important thing for the Thunder, as they, weakened by numerous injuries, finally returned to winning ways after two consecutive convincing defeats on the road.
 Steph Curry also shone, leading Golden State to a triumph over Phoenix (116:113) with 34 points, while Jamal Murray with 35 and Nikola Jokic with 26 points (he also had nine rebounds and eight assists) did not help Denver against Detroit.
 The Pistons won 118:110, with 28 points from Danny Avdija and 20 from Damian Lillard.
